docs.title: WTV Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the WTV documentation. This project provides tools for ion selection in mass spectrometry data based on the WTV-2.0 algorithm.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Command-line interface (CLI) for easy usage
  • Library functions for programmatic access
  • Support for MSP file format
  • Configurable parameters for different use cases

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: uv sync --all-extras

docs.title: Running the CLI
docs.text: uv run wtv-cli --msp_path input.msp --outpath ./output --mz_min 35 --mz_max 400

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:

docs.title: Acknowledgements
docs.text: This project is based on the original work by Honglun Yuan et al., published in WTV_2.0.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: This document provides an overview of the main modules and functions in the wtv library.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
• wtv.utils - Utility functions for MSP file I/O and data processing
  • wtv.ion_selection - Core ion selection algorithms
  • wtv.similarity - Similarity calculation functions

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from wtv.ion_selection import run_ion_selection

run_ion_selection(
    msp_file_path=Path("input.msp"),
    output_directory=Path("output"),
)

docs.title: API Reference: Ion Selection
docs.text: This document describes the ion selection functions in wtv.ion_selection.

docs.title: run_ion_selection
docs.text: Main function for performing ion selection on MSP files.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description msp_file_path Path Required Path to the input MSP file output_directory Path Required Directory to save the output files mz_min float 0 Minimum m/z value mz_max float inf Maximum m/z value rt_window float 1 Retention time window for finding nearby compounds min_ion_intensity_percent float 5 Minimum ion intensity percentage min_ion_num int 3 Minimum number of ions required prefer_mz_threshold float 150 Preferred m/z threshold similarity_threshold float 0.85 Similarity threshold for compound matching fr_factor float 2 Fragment ratio factor retention_time_max float inf Maximum retention time

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from wtv.ion_selection import run_ion_selection

run_ion_selection(
    msp_file_path=Path("input.msp"),
    output_directory=Path("output"),
    mz_min=35,
    mz_max=400,
    rt_window=2.00,
    min_ion_intensity_percent=7,
    min_ion_num=2,
    prefer_mz_threshold=60,
    similarity_threshold=0.85,
    fr_factor=2.0,
    retention_time_max=68.80,
)

docs.title: API Reference: Similarity
docs.text: This document describes the similarity calculation functions in wtv.similarity.

docs.title: dot_product_distance
docs.text: Calculate the dot product distance between two vectors.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description p np.ndarray First vector q np.ndarray Second vector

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • float: Dot product distance between the two vectors (0 to 1)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from wtv.similarity import dot_product_distance

p = np.array([1, 2, 3])
q = np.array([4, 5, 6])
score = dot_product_distance(p, q)
print(f"Similarity score: {score}")

docs.title: weighted_dot_product_distance
docs.text: Calculate the weighted dot product distance with fragment ratio consideration.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description compare_df pd.DataFrame DataFrame with two columns representing vectors to compare fr_factor float Factor used in the FR calculation

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • float: Composite score based on weighted dot product distance and fragment ratio

docs.title: calculate_similarity
docs.text: Calculate similarity scores between a target compound and all compounds in a DataFrame.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description target_name str Name of the target compound df pd.DataFrame DataFrame containing compound data fr_factor float Factor used in the weighted dot product distance calculation

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • pd.DataFrame: DataFrame containing similarity scores for each compound

docs.title: calculate_average_score_and_difference_count
docs.text: Calculate the average similarity score and difference count for a targeted compound.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description targeted_compound str Name of the targeted compound ion_combination list List of ion combinations for similarity calculation df pd.DataFrame DataFrame containing compound data similarity_threshold float Similarity threshold for considering compounds as similar fr_factor float Factor used in the weighted dot product distance calculation

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • pd.DataFrame: DataFrame containing difference counts and average similarity scores

docs.title: calculate_combination_score
docs.text: Calculate the combination score for ion combinations.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description combination_df pd.DataFrame DataFrame containing ion combinations targeted_compound str Name of the targeted compound temp_df pd.DataFrame Temporary DataFrame containing compound data prefer_mz_threshold float Preferred m/z threshold

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • pd.DataFrame: DataFrame with combination scores added

docs.title: calculate_solo_compound_combination_score
docs.text: Calculate the combination score for solo compounds.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description matrix_1 pd.DataFrame DataFrame containing solo compound data prefer_mz_threshold float Preferred m/z threshold

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • pd.DataFrame: DataFrame with combination scores added and sorted by score

docs.title: API Reference: Utils
docs.text: This document describes the utility functions in wtv.utils.

docs.title: read_msp
docs.text: Reads an MSP file and returns metadata and retention time data using matchms.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description msp_file_path str or Path Required Path to the MSP file retention str "retention_time" Name of the retention field

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
• Tuple[Dict[str, Dict[float, int]], pd.DataFrame]:
  • Dictionary of compound names to ion intensities
  • DataFrame with columns 'Name' and 'RT'

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from wtv.utils import read_msp

meta, rt_data = read_msp("input.msp")
print(meta.keys())  # Compound names
print(rt_data)      # Retention times

docs.title: write_msp
docs.text: Writes filtered ions to an MSP file.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description ion_df pd.DataFrame DataFrame containing ion data with 'RT' and 'ion' columns output_directory Path Directory to save the output MSP file source_msp_file Path Path to the source MSP file

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from wtv.utils import write_msp

write_msp(ion_df, Path("output"), Path("input.msp"))

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: • Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]: RT_data and ion matrix

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text: The WTV CLI provides an easy way to perform ion selection on mass spectrometry data.

docs.title: Basic Command
docs.text:
wtv-cli --msp_path input.msp --outpath output --mz_min 35 --mz_max 400 ...

When using uv:

uv run wtv-cli --msp_path input.msp --outpath output ...

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description Default --msp_path Path to the input MSP file. Required --outpath Directory to save the output files. Required --mz_min Minimum m/z value. 35 --mz_max Maximum m/z value. 400 --rt_window Retention time window. 2.00 --min_ion_intensity_percent Minimum ion intensity percentage. 7 --min_ion_num Minimum number of ions. 2 --prefer_mz_threshold Preferred m/z threshold. 60 --similarity_threshold Similarity threshold. 0.85 --fr_factor FR factor. 2.0 --retention_time_max Maximum retention time. 68.80

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
Run ion selection with default parameters:

wtv-cli \
    --msp_path input.msp \
    --outpath ./output \
    --mz_min 35 \
    --mz_max 400 \
    --rt_window 2.0 \
    --min_ion_intensity_percent 7 \
    --min_ion_num 2 \
    --prefer_mz_threshold 60 \
    --similarity_threshold 0.85 \
    --fr_factor 2.0 \
    --retention_time_max 68.80

docs.title: Custom Parameters
docs.text:
Adjust parameters for your specific data:

wtv-cli \
    --msp_path my_data.msp \
    --outpath ./results \
    --mz_min 50 \
    --mz_max 500 \
    --rt_window 1.5 \
    --similarity_threshold 0.9

docs.title: Using with uv
docs.text:
If you installed with uv, run:

uv run wtv-cli --msp_path input.msp --outpath ./output --mz_min 35 --mz_max 400

docs.title: Output
docs.text: The CLI generates an MSP file in the specified output directory containing the filtered spectra based on the ion selection algorithm.

docs.title: Using uv (Recommended)
docs.text:
1. Install uv if you haven't already: ```bash # Using pip pip install uv

# Or using Homebrew on macOS brew install uv

# Or using curl curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh ```

  1. Clone the repository: bash git clone https://github.com/RECETOX/wtv.git cd wtv

  2. Sync dependencies and create virtual environment: bash uv sync --all-extras

This will: - Create a virtual environment in .venv - Install all dependencies including dev and docs extras - Make the wtv-cli command available

docs.title: Common uv Commands
docs.text: Command Description uv sync Sync dependencies (install packages) uv sync --all-extras Install all optional dependencies uv run <command> Run a command in the virtual environment uv add <package> Add a new dependency uv build Build distribution packages

docs.title: Using pip
docs.text:
1. Install the library directly from PyPI: bash pip install wtv

  2. For development, clone the repository and install in editable mode: bash git clone https://github.com/RECETOX/wtv.git cd wtv pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Run the following command to verify the installation:

wtv-cli --help

You should see the CLI help message with available options.

docs.title: Library Usage
docs.text: The WTV library provides programmatic access to its core functionality for ion selection in mass spectrometry data.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
First, install the library:

uv sync --all-extras

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text:
Run ion selection using the run_ion_selection function:

from pathlib import Path
from wtv.ion_selection import run_ion_selection

run_ion_selection(
    msp_file_path=Path("input.msp"),
    output_directory=Path("output"),
    mz_min=35,
    mz_max=400,
    rt_window=2.00,
    min_ion_intensity_percent=7,
    min_ion_num=2,
    prefer_mz_threshold=60,
    similarity_threshold=0.85,
    fr_factor=2.0,
    retention_time_max=68.80,
)

docs.title: run_ion_selection
docs.text:
Main function for performing ion selection on MSP files.

Parameters: - msp_file_path (Path): Path to the input MSP file - output_directory (Path): Directory to save output - mz_min (float): Minimum m/z value (default: 0) - mz_max (float): Maximum m/z value (default: infinity) - rt_window (float): Retention time window for finding nearby compounds (default: 1) - min_ion_intensity_percent (float): Minimum ion intensity percentage (default: 5) - min_ion_num (int): Minimum number of ions required (default: 3) - prefer_mz_threshold (float): Preferred m/z threshold (default: 150) - similarity_threshold (float): Similarity threshold for compound matching (default: 0.85) - fr_factor (float): Fragment ratio factor (default: 2) - retention_time_max (float): Maximum retention time (default: infinity)

Example:

from pathlib import Path
from wtv.ion_selection import run_ion_selection

# Run with custom parameters
run_ion_selection(
    msp_file_path=Path("data/sample.msp"),
    output_directory=Path("results"),
    mz_min=50,
    mz_max=500,
    rt_window=1.5,
    similarity_threshold=0.9,
)

docs.title: generate_ion_combinations
docs.text:
Generate optimal ion combinations for compounds.

Parameters: - min_ion_intensity_percent: Minimum ion intensity percentage - min_ion_num: Minimum number of ions - prefer_mz_threshold: Preferred m/z threshold - similarity_threshold: Similarity threshold - fr_factor: Fragment ratio factor - RT_data: DataFrame with retention time data - matrix: DataFrame with ion intensities - rt_window: Retention time window

Example:

from wtv.utils import load_data
from wtv.ion_selection import generate_ion_combinations

# Load data
RT_data, matrix = load_data(Path("input.msp"), mz_min=35, mz_max=400)

# Generate ion combinations
combinations = generate_ion_combinations(
    min_ion_intensity_percent=7,
    min_ion_num=2,
    prefer_mz_threshold=60,
    similarity_threshold=0.85,
    fr_factor=2.0,
    RT_data=RT_data,
    matrix=matrix,
    rt_window=2.0,
)

docs.title: Data Loading
docs.text:
from wtv.utils import load_data, read_msp, create_ion_matrix

# Load data from MSP file
RT_data, matrix = load_data(Path("input.msp"), mz_min=35, mz_max=400)

# Or use read_msp directly
ion_dict, rt_df = read_msp("input.msp")

docs.title: Writing Results
docs.text:
from wtv.utils import write_msp

# Write filtered spectra to MSP file
write_msp(ion_rt_df, Path("output"), Path("input.msp"))

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
The library uses Python's logging module. To see detailed logs:

import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)

from wtv.ion_selection import run_ion_selection
run_ion_selection(...)
